title: What Time Is It?
subtitle: Four conversations about the time
review: Draft written by Claude. Check the text before recording audio. No Burmese yet.
intro: Anna and Tom's day, from seven in the morning to eleven at night. Listen for the time in each conversation, then say it with them.

lines.note: 7:00. We say o'clock only when the time is exactly on the hour.

lines.text: Your bus is at eight. Get up, please.
lines.note: at + a time: at eight, at seven o'clock.
11:30. You can also say eleven thirty.

lines.text: Oh no. Thirty more minutes! I'm hungry.
At four o'clock, in the park.
I finish work at four. Is a quarter past four OK?
Yes, a quarter past four is fine.
Great. See you at the park!
Anna, can we watch one more show?
No, Tom. Look at the clock. What time is it?

lines.note: 10:45. To = before: fifteen minutes before eleven.

lines.text: Yes, and we get up at six o'clock.

notes: What time is it? asks for the time now. The answer starts with It's: It's seven o'clock.
What time is lunch? asks when something happens. The answer uses at: Lunch is at twelve o'clock.
past = after the hour: half past eleven (11:30), a quarter past four (4:15).
to = before the next hour: a quarter to eleven (10:45).
o'clock is only for the exact hour: seven o'clock, but half past seven.

questions.q: What time does Tom wake up?
It is half past eleven. Lunch is at twelve o'clock. How long do Tom and Anna wait?
questions.why: Half past eleven is 11:30. Tom says: Thirty more minutes!

questions.q: What time do Anna and Tom meet at the park?
questions.why: Tom finishes work at four, so they meet at a quarter past four (4:15).

questions.q: Tom says: It's a quarter to eleven. What time is it?
questions.why: A quarter to eleven = fifteen minutes before eleven.
